items.title: RT-SYS-1
items.problem: The shared evaluate.newey_west_t uses lag = floor(4 (n/100)^(2/9)): 8 lags for 3,500 hourly rows, 10 for 13,000. Hourly loss or return series with daily / weekly seasonality or multi-day overlapping labels need far longer lags or block aggregation. It happened not to matter for TVTP (RT-TVTP-1), but every hourly study using it inherits the risk.

items.problem: The only direction effect (first touch of the prior-day / prior-week high or low continues: +0.15-0.33 sigma vs placebo) is a tail, not a hit rate (continuation probability 0.46-0.49, same as placebo), 5-8 bp against about 15 bp of round-trip costs, and every executable rule built on it loses (H-GEO16, DSR 0 over 2,576 trials). items.title: RT-PART-1
items.problem: 'Informedness' is the 60 s markout side x (mid(t+60 s) - execution price) relative to the all-order mean. It includes each order's own permanent price impact and is not size-matched, while the types are defined by size, levels crossed and burst traits; the sweepers' +0.84 bp may be own impact of large multi-level orders rather than information. Registry-wide the result is robust statistically (t 13-22 over days), so the issue is interpretation, not significance.
items.suggested_test: Before using types to decide whom to quote against: markout from the post-trade mid (t + 1 s) to t + 60 s and a within-type regression on log(notional / L1); report permanent vs temporary impact.
